Walking tracks around the village include the Tronoh Dredge hole circuit and the East Ovens River Track

name: Tronoh Dredge Walking Track

facts.claim: Roughly 1.4-1.5 km loop around the dredge hole, a man-made lake, about 30 min
Tronoh Dredge was one of the world's largest electric-powered dredges, operating 1942 to 1954
Starts at Tronoh Dredge car park off Feathertop Track; reserve is run by volunteer committees, not Parks Victoria

ticketUrl_note: community-managed reserve, no official site found

name: Mount Beauty Gorge Walk

facts.claim: Track from Big Hill Mountain Bike Park via the Aqueduct Track about 1 km to a swing bridge over the West Kiewa River
Beyond the bridge is a swimming hole and the 1950s adit dug for the Kiewa hydro scheme
In dry summer you can wade and swim 400 m upstream to a canyon; river levels can rise suddenly because it is part of the hydro scheme

ticketUrl_note: no single steward; tourism listing only
access_note: Water flows may rise without warning (hydro scheme)

name: Old Beechworth Gaol

facts.claim: Completed in 1864; held Ned Kelly, his brother Dan, and Ellen Kelly; closed in 2004
Built of granite quarried on site; part of the Beechworth Historic Precinct on the National Heritage List
Guided tours about 45 minutes, run daily
